questions.answer: The two Eids are the biggest for us, along with cultural events like Pohela Boishakh, the Bengali New Year. They're wonderful occasions, full of food, family and colour, and the whole community becomes [[vibrant]].

questions.q: Which festival do you enjoy the most?
questions.answer: Eid-ul-Fitr, without a doubt. After a month of fasting, there's a wonderful sense of relief and joy, and the whole family comes together, often at our village home. The [[jubilant]] mood lasts for days.

questions.q: How do you usually celebrate special occasions?
questions.answer: Usually with family and a large meal, which is really at the heart of any celebration here. We dress up, visit relatives, and the day is loud, lively and warm. Food is always the [[centrepiece]].

questions.q: How did you celebrate festivals when you were a child?
questions.answer: Eid was the highlight of my year. I'd get new clothes, and older relatives would give us salami, a small gift of money. My cousins and I would compare how much we'd collected, which was [[fiercely competitive]].

questions.q: Do you think festivals have changed over the years?
questions.answer: In some ways, yes. People now send greetings online instead of visiting everyone in person, and celebrations have become more [[commercialised]], with lots of shopping. But the core of it, family and food, has stayed exactly the same.
